teach.heading: Every candle has body parts.
teach.body: The candle body shows the distance between the open and close. The wick shows where price traveled but did not fully hold. The high and low show the full range of that candle. A wick does not automatically mean reversal — it means price reached that area and did not close there. Context tells you what that rejection means.
teach.dayliNote: "A wick shows me where price went. A close shows me where price accepted. That difference matters." — Dayli Scott

experience.intro: Practice separating what a wick shows from what a close shows.

steps.prompt: A candle has a huge high-to-low range but its open and close are nearly identical. Large body or small body?

options.label: Small body — despite the wide range, price didn't settle far from where it started
options.feedback: Right — body size comes from open-to-close distance, not the full range.

options.label: Large body — a wide range always means a large body
options.feedback: Range and body size are different measurements — a wide range can still have a tiny body.

steps.prompt: Price wicks above resistance but the candle closes back below it. Did price "break" resistance?

options.label: No — it reached above but didn't close above, so it didn't accept the break
options.feedback: Right — reaching isn't the same as accepting.

options.label: Yes — any candle touching above resistance counts as a break
options.feedback: Touching a level and closing through it are different claims — only the close shows acceptance.

steps.prompt: You're trying to decide whether price "held" a level. Should you look at the wick or the close?

options.label: The close — it shows where price actually settled
options.feedback: Exactly. The wick shows travel, the close shows acceptance.

options.label: The wick — it shows the full extreme reached
options.feedback: The wick shows how far price traveled, not whether it actually held there.

reinforce.question: A candle has a huge range from high to low, but its open and close are almost identical. Is that a large-bodied candle or a small-bodied one — and what does that tell you?
options: Small-bodied — despite the wide range, price didn't settle far from where it started, showing indecision inside the candle
Large-bodied — a wide high-to-low range always means a large body
It's impossible to know the body size without the color

reinforce.question: Explain the difference between what a candle's wick tells you and what its close tells you.
reinforce.modelAnswer: The wick shows the full extent of where price traveled during that candle — the extreme it reached but didn't hold. The close shows where price actually settled by the end of the period — what buyers and sellers ultimately agreed on. A wick shows reach; a close shows acceptance, and they can point in different directions on the same candle.

reinforce.question: Price wicks above resistance but closes below it — that means it reached above but did not ___ above.
